chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Asbat ibn Salim, from Ala' ibn Kamil who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'It is upon you to supplicate, for it is a healing from every illness.'

key_terms.داء: Da': illness, disease, ailment — encompasses physical and spiritual maladies
key_terms.شفاء: Shifa': healing, cure — used for both bodily and spiritual ailments
key_terms.عليك بالدعاء: It is upon you to do supplication — an imperative exhortation formula in hadith

ai.seo_question: Is supplication (du'a) a cure for illness in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) personally urged his companion Ala' ibn Kamil to make du'a (supplication), describing it as a comprehensive cure for every ailment. This teaching was addressed to an individual companion in a direct, personal manner—'he said to me'—which gives it the character of personal spiritual counsel. In the early Islamic tradition, 'illness' (da') encompasses both physical ailments and spiritual diseases such as negligence of God, pride, and despair.
